title: std::string_view (part 2)
recap: A std::string owns its data, while std::string_view only observes data owned elsewhere. A view becomes dangling when its source is destroyed and is commonly invalidated when an owning std::string is modified.

remove_prefix() and remove_suffix() narrow a view without changing the underlying string. Returning a view into a caller-owned argument is safe when the caller keeps that owner alive and unchanged for every later use of the returned view.
objectives: Keep an owning std::string alive while a view and returned slice refer to it.
Return a std::string_view parameter rather than a view into a local string.
Slice without allocation using remove_prefix() and remove_suffix().
Avoid modifying the owner while derived views are in use.
warnings: A std::string_view does not extend the lifetime of the string it views.
Returning a view into a local std::string or storing a view of a temporary std::string creates a dangling view.
Modifying an owning std::string can invalidate every view into its character storage.
challenge: Keep trimBrackets() taking and returning std::string_view, and narrow its local view by one character on each side with remove_prefix() and remove_suffix(). Preserve the supplied named std::string owner so source and slice both refer to live, unchanged storage while they are printed. A direct view of a string literal would also be lifetime-safe because literals have static storage duration, but this exercise practices the caller-owned string case.
hints: A view is not an owner; the supplied named std::string owns [stable slice] for the full duration of both output statements.
Keep source initialized from owner, then pass source to trimBrackets so the returned view still refers into the live owner.
Inside trimBrackets, call text.remove_prefix(1) and text.remove_suffix(1) before returning text; do not modify owner afterward.
